structure: Oklahoma Academic Standards for Social Studies (2025), one PDF of 179 pages, all content in tables (T1/T2). Front matter (cover, TOC, Introduction, Standards Overview, Content Strands Overview, Social Studies Practices Overview) precedes the grade/course sections. Then one section per grade level (Pre-Kindergarten, Kindergarten, Grades 1-8) and one per high-school course (Oklahoma History and Government, Modern World History, United States History, United States Government, Economics, World Geography, Ancient and Medieval World History, History of 20th Century Totalitarianism, Psychology, Sociology), each starting with a title cell ('Grade N Social Studies: <theme>' or the course title), a short overview narrative (what students study), then 'Practice Standards: Grades X-Y' and '<Grade/Course> Content Standards'. PK has only content standards (no practice block) with codes PK.n (strand) and PK.n.m (objective). Grades K-8 and the HS courses have two blocks: Practice Standards (code <grade>.P.n strand, <grade>.P.n.m objective with lettered sub-items A-D; strands P.1 Democratic processes, P.2 disciplinary tools, P.3 critical reading, P.4 writing/research) and Content Standards (<grade>.C.n strand statement 'The student will ...', <grade>.C.n.m objective with lettered sub-items A, B, C...). Course codes: OKH, MWH, USH, USG, E, WG, AWH, TOT, PS, S (+ .P. / .C.); course practice standards (OKH.P etc.) are repeated verbatim in each course with the 9-12 wording. The practice blocks in K/1, 2/3, 4/5 and 6/7/8 repeat the same band wording under each grade's own code (K.P / 1.P etc.), so each copy gets its single grade. Table layout: strand statement in column 1 (C1) and objectives in a later column (C2-C4); header cells ('X Content Standards', grade title) in C1/C2; long rows are split across page breaks so a continuation fragment (no code, starts mid-sentence or with 'B.', 'C.') belongs to the same standard/strand as the preceding unit. No separate example/teacher-note blocks exist; examples (e.g., ...) and lettered sub-items are inside the standard text and are labeled standards. Only the grade/course overview narrative is 'examples'. The final Appendix: Social Studies Practices (PK-12) is a grade-band table (T1/T2): columns K-Grade 1, Grades 2-3, Grades 4-5, Grades 6-8, Grades 9-12; each cell begins 'A. (K-1)', 'B. (2-3)' etc. giving the band, with practice titles I-IV and numbered practice statements spanning all grades; labeled standards with the grade band of each cell and PK-12 for the titles/statements.

Practice Standards blocks are repeated per grade under their own code (e.g. K.P and 1.P both under 'Practice Standards: Grades K-1'; 2.P/3.P under 'Grades 2-3'; 4.P/5.P; 6.P/7.P/8.P). Each copy is labeled with the single grade of its section/code, not the band; headers u107, u165, u234, u312, u368, u424, u511, u591, u677 likewise take the section's grade.

High-school course practice standards (OKH.P, MWH.P, USH.P, USG.P, E.P, WG.P, AWH.P, TOT.P) are course-specific verbatim copies; labeled course=<course>, grades 9-12, cat standards. The Psychology and Sociology sections have no practice block.
